answer: Epoch-bound verifiable delay functions resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to evaluate a sequential proof over its public key and a fresh randomness beacon every round. Rather than drifting like a zephyr through a nebula of free keys, each identity hits a basalt wall of non-parallelizable compute, forcing attackers to spend dedicated core-time and energy per clone. However, adversaries with custom ASICs or cloud budgets can still provision parallel hardware.
